role_owner_hint: Administers the organization: people, access, integrations
role_admin_hint: A member an owner may later grant more to
confidence_confirmed_hint: Proved by the provider; activity on it counts as theirs
confidence_claimed_hint: They say it is theirs; not proved yet, so nothing is attributed
confidence_suggested_hint: Studio guessed it; nobody has confirmed it
org_about: One tenant per organization (the admin hierarchy governs management, never data); workspaces and members live inside it. Switch organizations in the path bar.
org_same_name_hint: Another organization has the same name
org_create_about: An organization is a tenant in the admin hierarchy — your workspaces, members and repositories will live inside it.
org_create_hint: Created managed (platform admins keep access); it can request self-managed mode later via dual consent.
org_mode_hint: Dual-consent mode conversion: creates a pending request the other side approves
org_requested_inside_hint: Self-managed = visibility barrier. An admin homed inside this organization requests the conversion; you approve it here.
org_self_managed_confirm: This raises a VISIBILITY BARRIER: you (and every platform admin) lose access to the organization and everything inside it — its workspaces disappear from your lists. Only an admin whose home is inside the organization can request the conversion back to managed; you would then approve it here.
org_delete_about: Permanently deletes the tenant. Its workspaces must be deleted first (the platform refuses to cascade); Keycloak users keep existing.
org_access_map_about: Your scope is your home tenant's subtree. Self-managed is a visibility barrier: that subtree is governed by its own admins and hidden from you.
org_barrier_hint: Visibility barrier: governed by its own admins; only a dual-consent conversion (requested from inside) lifts it
org_access_map_enforcement: Enforcement today: scope + barriers only — fine-grained permissions are registered in the types-registry but the PDP is not wired yet (allow-all).
logo_about: Shown beside the name in the path bar and the organization switcher. PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, at most 256 KiB.
logo_bad_type: Pick a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF image.
logo_too_big: The logo is {size} KiB; at most {max} KiB is kept.
people_pick_org: Pick an organization to see its members.
people_about: Who belongs to this organization and in what role. Only an active owner administers it; the last one cannot be demoted, suspended or removed.
people_empty: Nobody belongs to this organization yet.
people_only_owner: The only active owner: add another owner first
people_remove_body: They leave the organization, and their personal connections here go with them.
people_add_platform_hint: Platform admin: Add puts someone with an identity in now, whether or not they have signed in yet.
people_directory_unavailable: The directory of people is not available on this Studio ({error}) — invite them by e-mail instead.
people_invite_hint: An invitation is seen when they sign in with that address; they accept it themselves.
people_withdraw_body: The link stops working. They can be invited again.
dir_hint: Every member of the organization sees this description.
ids_person_hint: The canonical person id every membership and grant keys on
ids_no_logins: No sign-in method resolves to this person — they were added before anyone signed in as them.
ids_no_aliases: No external account is attributed to this person yet.
access_about: Choose how access works in {name}. Stored on the organization (like the automation level); enforcement arrives with the Studio PDP.
access_self_managed: {name} is self-managed. It raises a visibility barrier — its access is governed by admins inside the organization, and it can't be configured from here. Convert it to managed (requested from inside, via dual consent) to manage its access on this screen.
access_model_tenant_blurb: Access follows membership: anyone in an organization or project can act within it. Simple, no roles to manage.
access_model_roles_blurb: Access is granted through roles — each role is a set of privileges — assigned to members and teams. Fine-grained, but you manage roles.
access_rolling_out: Enforcement is rolling out. The Studio PDP now filters a project's Works by these grants (ADR-0009); other surfaces still run allow-all until their checks land. Owner keeps every privilege.
access_no_grant: You have no grant here. With role-based access on, you'd be locked out of this organization's projects.
access_grants_about: Assign a role to a member or a team, scoped to the whole organization or a single project. This is the (subject × role × scope) the PDP will read.
access_no_grants: No grants yet — add one below.
access_tenant_on: Tenant access is on: anyone who is a member of the organization or a project can act within it. Switch to Role-based access above to define roles and privileges.
secrets_about: Repository credentials in the credstore gear. Values are write-only; this view lists the references known to this organization's workspace settings and connections, probes their health, and rotates broken ones (the store has no list API — anything saved outside the portal won't appear here).
secrets_empty: No secret references found in any workspace settings.
secrets_broken_hint: Exists but unreadable (or missing) — rotate to heal
secrets_delete_body: Project settings keep the reference, and launches clone without credentials until a new value is saved.
secrets_new_value: New value, e.g. a fresh PAT
objects_about: Every type the graph stores for this organization. Tick one and it becomes a component: the Components page lists its nodes, against the field schema the type has, or the gear schema if it has none of its own. Untick it and it leaves. The nodes are untouched either way: a mark is an opinion about a type, not a change to what is stored under it.
objects_about_counts: Objects counts the nodes of each type in this organization's graph. graph-storage has no count in its contract, so the number is taken by paging and stops at 2 000; past that it reads 2 000+, which is also where the Components page stops rendering.
objects_empty: The graph has no node types yet.
objects_empty_hint: Run a sync, or ingest an artifact.
objects_no_match: No type matches the current filter.
objects_companion: Studio keeps this beside a component; it is not one of its own
objects_no_nodes_hint: Marked, but the graph holds no node of it yet
objects_capped: More than {count} — the count stops there, and so does the Components page
ids_about: Everyone whose identity exists in Studio Keycloak, including people waiting for organization access.
ids_about_audit: This is an identity directory, not an OAuth failure log. A rejected login that never created a Keycloak identity belongs in the security audit instead.
ids_drift_hint: The IdP attribute is not rewritten when a membership changes
ids_admin_everywhere: Administers every organization. Add them to one on its People screen.
tenants_about: The raw tenant list behind the projects — one AM tenant of type workspace per project. Concept v2 does not show this level; it is here so the hierarchy stays administrable.
tenants_empty: No workspaces yet — create the first one below.
tenants_no_match: No workspaces match the current filters.
int_no_org: No organization to hold the shared catalogue yet.
int_about: What {name} connects to and shares with its projects. Configure one once, then pick repositories from a list instead of pasting clone URLs.
int_about_tokens: Tokens go to credstore — after you submit one the browser never sees it again. Your personal connections are on your profile.
int_empty_body: “+ Add connection” starts with a provider.
int_remove_body: The connection and its stored token go. Sources attached through it stop syncing.
int_remove_shared_body: It is shared with your other projects, and removing it here removes it there too — with its token.
int_missing_source_code: no repository can be attached or synced
int_missing_ai: the IDE agents and chat run only on personal keys
int_missing_notification: Studio cannot tell anyone what happened
int_no_drivers: No connector driver plugin is registered in this build.
int_blurb_source_code: Repositories Studio reads: browse them and attach them to projects.
int_blurb_ai: Keys the IDE agents and chat run on — Anthropic for Claude Code, OpenAI for Codex — for anyone without a key in their profile: a personal one for you, a workspace one for this workspace, an organization one for every workspace in it.
int_blurb_notification: Where Studio tells people what happened: Slack, Zulip or Discord. A bot token reaches every channel it was invited to; an incoming webhook posts to the one channel its URL was created for.
int_blurb_cluster: Kubernetes clusters the organization's environments deploy into: the API server and a service-account token, or a kubeconfig with the cluster's CA. Only the server uses it — connect it for the organization, not personally.
int_blurb_registry: Container registries the organization's products are published to and its clusters pull from: the address and username:token. Only the server uses it — connect it for the organization, not personally.
int_blurb_compute: Platforms that build and run your products on hardware they allocate: Constructor Research. You sign in with your Constructor account; no password or key is pasted here.
int_research_pending: not set up on this Studio yet
int_research_pending_title: This Studio is not registered with the Constructor sign-in yet, or does not know Research's address: the platform administrator sets it up.
int_research_pending_why: Constructor Research appears here once this Studio is registered with the Constructor sign-in and knows Research's integration service. Then: sign in with your Constructor account, and add an environment that runs on Research.
int_reach_personal: Only me — private to my account
int_reach_org_hint: Stored once and inherited by every project; the token is readable across them.
int_reach_personal_hint: Stored here, but the token stays readable only by you.
int_webhook_hint: The webhook URL below is the whole address: host, channel and secret. Nothing else to configure.
int_url_ai: Leave empty for {url} — or any compatible endpoint
int_url_notification: Leave empty for {url} — or your own installation
int_url_self_hosted: Leave empty for {url} — or your self-hosted installation
int_credstore_hint: Stored in credstore under a per-connection reference. Never logged, never returned by the API.
int_kubeconfig_or_paste: or paste a token or a kubeconfig below
int_signin_hint: You will sign in with your Constructor account — Google, Microsoft or a password, the way you always do. Studio never sees the password; it keeps only an access key you can revoke by removing this connection.
int_signin_only_you: Only you can use it: it is your own account.
int_edit_token: New token (leave empty to keep the current one)
int_edit_hint: The change is verified against the provider before anything is stored, with or without a new token. The connection id is preserved, so project sources keep working.
int_updated: Connection updated — the credential belongs to {account}
int_updated_unnamed: Connection updated — the credential belongs to an unnamed account
int_share_title: How “Share with the team” in the IDE lands edits in these repositories
int_attached_one: Attached {count} repository to {name} — cloned on the next session launch.
int_attached_many: Attached {count} repositories to {name} — cloned on the next session launch.
dm_about: The types this organization's screens show, and their fields. A field added here is a field of every object of the type at once; every change is a numbered model version on the server.
dm_about_origin: Each type says where it came from: Studio's core, a kit installed in the organization, a gear that keeps its records, an uploaded model, or this organization's own edit.
dm_no_types: This organization's model has no types.
dm_objects_hint: Objects of this type in this organization
dm_read_only: You can read the model. Changing it needs the organization administrator role.
dm_no_own_fields: No fields of its own yet. Add one, and every screen that shows this type shows it.
dm_held_hint: {gear} writes this field; add a field beside it instead
dm_remove_hint: Drop the field from the type. Stored values stay in the objects.
dm_no_relations: No relation to or from another type in this model.
dm_relations_hint: Right: what {name} points at. Left: what points at it. Choose a type to open it; a dashed line is a relation it inherits from a base.
dm_type_id_hint: Lower-case words joined by hyphens. It cannot change later.
dm_type_extends_hint: It inherits every field and relation of the type it extends.
